newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mixed before nuke restarts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mixed before nuke restarts.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Monday before the expected restarts of the two units at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) later this week, market sources said.
"We're waiting for new information to come in," said a Houston futures trader, referring to the market focus on SONGS' startup schedule.

Southern California Edison (SoCal Edison) today confirmed the 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear station in southern California was still set to begin putting electricity on grid tomorrow.
The adjacent 1,080 MW San Onofre unit 3 was scheduled to restart Thursday, SoCal Edison added.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 27 cents at $35.54 a megawatt hour (MWh). trimming a 73 cent gain.
September PV finished up 12 cents at $29.42. Deferred PV contracts ended flat to 15 cents higher.
August California-Oregon Border settled down 15 cents at $22.53 a MWh after bouncing in a 25 cent range.
September COB finished down 11 cents at $22.65. Other active COB months ended 10 to 15 cents lower.

Although triple-digit heat in the interior Southwest kept that region's air-conditioners humming and boosted day-ahead power prices, weather in southern California--the largest summer demand area in the West--was forecast to stay mild in the mid-80s F this week.
Day-ahead peak, firm power prices at the Palo Verde switchyard in Arizona climbed eight dollars to $38.00-40.00 a MWh, while those at COB rose to $17.75-18.25 from Friday's $15.50-17.00.
Traders said near-term direction of the futures complex would track closely with news of the progress (or possible setback) of the SONGS units coming back to service.
"Until that happens, nothing much is going to happen," the Houston trader said.
Besides the SONGS restarts, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was operating at 42 percent power Monday and set to hit full power midweek after repairs.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was shut Friday for three weeks for repairs.
Restarts of the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming and the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired plant in Nevada were postponed to Wenesday.

The Pacific Northwest was expected to see readings rising to one to five degrees Fahrenheit above normal with a chance of showers midweek, while the Southwest would continue to experience dry and seasonal hot weather.
NYMEX estimated 246 COB and 410 PV contracts were sold.
